messages:
sasha: Quick idea — trying a conservative prefetch + tiling heuristic for draft models. Goal: keep tail latency SLO while reclaiming some batching efficiency. Thoughts?

kyle: Sounds promising. By conservative you mean avoid fetching >1 tile ahead unless confidence > threshold?

sasha: Exactly. Rough sketch: compute a lightweight next-token confidence from the head logits; only prefetch KV tiles if confidence < 0.6 and remaining seq_len_in_tile > 4. Otherwise wait and rely on batching.

morgan: Can you paste the config sketch?

sasha: Sure:
```
prefetch:
  mode: conservative
  tile_size: 16
  lookahead_tiles: 1
  confidence_threshold: 0.6
  priority: ["prompt", "kv", "lm_head"]
  fallback: immediate_batch
```

joel: Two quick questions: (1) how expensive is the confidence calc per request? (2) does this interact poorly with 4-bit quantized KV caches?

sasha: Confidence is just a tiny softmax over top-k logits (k=8) — <200 FLOPs per request. For quantized KV, we might need a small warm-up read to avoid on-demand decode spikes; that's why tiling + priority ordering matters.

eva: From past experiments, conservative prefetch reduced p95 tail by ~18% but sometimes hurt throughput for short prompts. Do we have benchmarks for mixed prompt lengths?

sasha: Not yet. I propose an ablation matrix: tile_size ∈ {8,16,32}, lookahead ∈ {0,1,2}, confidence ∈ {0.5,0.6,0.75}, quant_mode ∈ {fp16, int8, nf4}. Measure: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and quality delta on heldout evals.

morgan: For quality—use our canonical prompt set + multi-turn dialog subset. Also include a short perplexity suite (unit prompts) to catch small regressions.

joel: How do we avoid biasing eval by the prefetch policy? If prefetch changes timing, user-visible outputs might differ because of nondeterminism in sampling seeds. Need fixed seeds and greedy baselines in the harness.

sasha: Agreed. Plan: for quality runs use deterministic sampling (top-k/top-p fixed) and seed control. For throughput/latency runs use production sampling. Split metrics accordingly.

morgan: Also add a canary config that enables optimistic prefetch for a tiny fraction of traffic so we can gather real-world signals. e.g., 0.5% canary.

sasha: Adding that — canary should route to dedicated small pool to avoid impacting main capacity.

joel: One more: instrument per-request tags so we can correlate prefetch decisions with downstream quality regressions (tag: prefetch_mode, tiles_prefetched, confidence_at_prefetch).

sasha: Will add tags.

devbot: Experiment job queued: ml-prefetch/tiling-probe-183980 — matrix 12 jobs. ETA ~3h for smallest tiles, ~10h full run. Logs at https://ci.redwood/models/183980/results

eva: Nice. Also, let's capture generation traces for a few failure cases (trace depth=200) so we can inspect KV alignment and whether partial prefetch caused hallucination spikes.

sasha: Good call. I'll attach trace hooks to any job where quality delta > 1.5% relative to baseline.

morgan: For the report, can we include a tiny microbenchmark: cost/token delta estimate (prefetch extra reads vs batching gains)? Ops team needs that to reason about Dedicated pricing.

sasha: Yep — I'll compute an amortized cost model: extra read bytes per token vs tokens/sec improvement -> $/1000 tokens estimate.

joel: Ok, next steps: run matrix, collect traces for flagged runs, produce short doc with perf/quality tradeoffs and canary rollout plan. Assign owners?

sasha: I'll own the matrix and analysis. @kyle can you own canary infra and tagging?

kyle: On it.

morgan: I'll prep the eval harness adjustments (seeded runs, greedy baselines).

joel: I'll review the report + sign off on canary.

sasha: Thanks team — kicking off now. :rocket:
